title: Supply chain hardening (npm hygiene + Claude Code hooks)
description: Harden the npm dependency surface and add the first Claude Code hooks for the harness. Motivated by the recent wave of npm supply-chain incidents (compromised maintainer accounts publishing malicious postinstall scripts, e.g. the s1ngularity / chalk-debug class of attacks). Adds three defensive layers: (1) `.npmrc` with `ignore-scripts=true`, `engine-strict=true`, and `minimum-release-age=7d` (npm 11.7+) — blocks the dominant attack vector and the recently-published-package window; (2) `npm audit` step in `init.sh` failing on moderate-or-higher, with the current 5 transitive CVEs resolved via `npm audit fix` and `overrides` where needed; (3) `.claude/settings.json` with hooks blocking out-of-band edits to `feature_list.json` and `package-lock.json`. Also pins Node/npm versions via `engines`, adds Dependabot config, documents the policy in `docs/conventions.md`, and updates `CHECKPOINTS.md`. Inserted at priority 0.5 — before `test-baseline` — so every subsequent feature inherits the hardening. RE-OPENED 2026-05-19 after the initial close: the Claude Code hooks shipped using a non-existent env var (`CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH`) and therefore never blocked anything. The reviewer's verification was synthetic (set the variable manually and confirmed the bash branch executed) but not end-to-end (never confirmed that Claude Code actually populates that variable). The correct mechanism is stdin JSON parsed via `jq` against `.tool_input.file_path`. This re-open ships the corrected hook, adds a real end-to-end verification recipe to `reviewer.md`, and updates `leader.md` to reflect that status rotations in `feature_list.json` will go through `jq`-driven Bash from now on (the hook will block direct Edit|Write).
acceptance: `.npmrc` exists with `ignore-scripts=true`, `engine-strict=true`, `minimum-release-age=7d`, and a comment block documenting the rationale for each setting.

An allowlist mechanism exists for legitimate postinstall scripts (esbuild today). Approach is documented in `docs/conventions.md` — current preferred form: explicit `npm rebuild esbuild` step in `init.sh` after `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.

`init.sh` adds: (a) `npm --version >= 11.7` sanity check, (b) explicit `npm ci` with `ignore-scripts` honoured (relies on `.npmrc`), (c) `npm rebuild` for the allowlisted packages, (d) `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` step failing the build on findings.

title: Fix GitHub Pages deploy after engine-strict policy
description: After feature 0.5 (supply-chain-hardening) introduced `engines: { node: '>=20', npm: '>=11.7' }` in package.json plus `engine-strict=true` in .npmrc, the GitHub Pages deploy workflow started failing on `npm ci` with EBADENGINE. The runner installs Node 20.18 (per .nvmrc) which ships with npm 10.8.2 — below the 11.7 floor we require. The fix is a single step in `.github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml` that bumps npm to 11.x immediately after `actions/setup-node`. title: Code-split routes with React.lazy + Suspense
description: The bundle has grown to 680.84 KB through the major dep bumps (vite/plugin-react, eslint, react). Vite's 500 KB warning fires on every build. This feature lazy-loads the heavy routes (`/new` NewGame and `/play` Play) with React.lazy + <Suspense>, dropping the initial bundle well below 500 KB and putting per-route chunks in dist/assets/. The WIP pages (/home, /login, /about) stay eager because they're trivial — splitting them would add chunk-loading overhead with no payload benefit. Inserted at priority 3.92 immediately after react-major-bump (3.9) — does bundle hygiene before any further code addition (especially the deferred react-chessboard 4→5 bump which would add ~50 KB to whatever chunk Play lives in).
acceptance: src/routes/Public.tsx imports NewGame and Play via React.lazy(() => import(...)) instead of eager imports. Error and WIP stay eager.

A <Suspense fallback={...}/> boundary wraps the lazy outlet. Fallback uses MUI components consistent with the rest of the app (likely a centered <CircularProgress />). Lives either in App.tsx around <Outlet /> or in Public.tsx as the route element wrapper — implementer picks the cleaner spot.

Existing tests still pass (49 expected). Tests that render NewGame or Play directly (via MemoryRouter etc.) may need an outer <Suspense> wrapper or await-style queries (findBy...) — implementer applies the minimum tweak needed. No tests removed or skipped.
dist/assets/ now contains at least 3 JS chunks: an initial chunk (App shell + theme + router + WIP page), a NewGame chunk, a Play chunk. Implementer reports the sizes.
Initial chunk drops well below 500 KB (no Vite chunk-size warning on the initial). Per-route chunks may individually be above their own thresholds but that's the point — they only load on navigation.
Total bundle size (sum of all JS chunks) should be roughly the same as before, possibly slightly larger due to chunk boundaries (small overhead). ±20 KB tolerance on the sum.
Dev server (`npm run dev`) and HMR still work end-to-end. Navigating between /home, /new, /play in the dev server triggers the lazy loads without stalls or crashes.

title: Bump react-chessboard 4 → 5 (semantic API migration)
description: Apply Dependabot PR #9 (react-chessboard 4.7.3 → 5.10.0). Unlike the other dep bumps in this series, this one requires a real semantic migration in pages/Play.tsx because the v4 → v5 transition collapsed the individual props (position, onPieceDrop, boardOrientation, areArrowsAllowed) into a single `options` object, renamed `areArrowsAllowed` to `allowDrawingArrows`, and changed the `onPieceDrop` callback signature from `(source, target) => boolean` to `({ piece, sourceSquare, targetSquare }) => boolean` with `targetSquare` now nullable (drag-off-board). title: Re-sync game state on STOMP reconnect (fix board divergence after restore-tab / sleep / network drop)
description: User reported reproducible bug 2026-05-27: after closing one of two playing tabs, restoring it via Ctrl+Shift+T (or after browser tab sleep / network drop) leaves the restored tab's chess.js in the initial position while the other tab keeps the real game state. The two clients then diverge silently — moves made on one side are rejected as 'not legal' on the other, and no banner / error surfaces the divergence. Root cause: feature 10's initial-load effect fetches GET /api/games/{gameId} once on mount (deps [gameId, ...]) and never re-fetches. The applyOpponentMove path silently drops MoveEvents that arrive before the initial GET resolves (with a comment promising 'the next GET will catch up' that is never honoured), and the STOMP client's built-in 5s reconnect doesn't trigger a re-fetch. Fix: observe useGameStomp's connectionState in Play.tsx; on any transition INTO Connected (from Disconnected / Reconnecting / Error), fire getGameState(gameId) + syncFromServer(state). Skip the first transition from Disconnected → Connected on initial mount (the initial-load effect already covers it). Backend is already the source of truth — no cross-repo work.
acceptance: src/pages/Play/Play.tsx adds a useEffect that observes useGameStomp's connectionState. On a transition INTO ConnectionState.Connected from any non-Connected state (Disconnected, Reconnecting, Error), fires `getGameState(gameId)` + `syncFromServer(state)`. The initial mount transition is gated so it does not double-fetch with the existing initial-load effect.

Gate strategy: a useRef<boolean> 'hasFetchedOnce' initialized to false; the initial-load effect flips it true on success; the connectionState-transition effect only fires when hasFetchedOnce && previousConnectionState !== Connected && currentConnectionState === Connected. Implementer may choose an equivalent guard if cleaner — document the choice in the feature note.

Error path: if the resync GET returns GAME_NOT_FOUND / GAME_ALREADY_ENDED, route to the existing 404-path (leaveRoom() + navigate('/new')). Other errors keep the user on the page with a Snackbar (do NOT redirect on transient network errors).

Race-condition handling: if a MoveEvent arrives via STOMP after the resync GET starts but before it resolves, applyOpponentMove still drops it when prev === null. After the resync GET resolves, state is correct (the GET response includes all moves up to that point). Confirm the existing `applyOpponentMove` early-return on `prev === null` is still safe and remove the misleading 'next GET will catch up' comment in favour of a comment that points to the new resync effect.

Tests (Vitest): connectionState transition from Reconnecting → Connected fires a second getGameState call; transition Disconnected → Connected on initial mount does NOT double-fire (only the initial-load effect runs); GAME_NOT_FOUND on resync navigates to /new and clears session; resync after a move-in-flight reconciles to the latest server state; previousConnectionState ref does not leak across unmount/remount.

E2E (Playwright): new spec or extension of an existing one that simulates a STOMP disconnect mid-game (close + reopen the WS connection via mockStomp helper), opponent makes a move during the disconnect, then asserts the restored client's board reflects the move after reconnect. Use the existing mockStomp's onClose hook + a new onReconnect helper if needed.

title: Fix board not syncing after Ctrl+Shift+T (tab restore via session-restore bfcache)
description: User reported reproducible bug 2026-05-28 after smoke-testing features 10/11/11.1/11.5 in production. Restoring a closed game tab via Ctrl+Shift+T leaves the board in initial position instead of the current game state. Forensic via DevTools (performance.getEntriesByType) confirmed: (1) sessionStorage rehydrates correctly with gameId; (2) initial-load effect fires GET /api/games/{gameId} with transferSize=0, duration ~10-23ms — signature of an AbortController-aborted request; (3) navigation.type === 'back_forward' (session restore, not pure bfcache); (4) backend serves correct state when re-fetched manually. Root cause hypothesis: under back_forward navigation, the interaction between React 19 concurrent rendering, the React.lazy + Suspense boundary on Play route (feature 3.92), and the initial-load effect's AbortController causes the cleanup to fire transiently mid-fetch, aborting the GET. Feature 11.1's resync-on-Connected was supposed to be the safety net but its initial-mount suppression (intentional, to avoid double-fetch with initial-load) means it does NOT fire on first STOMP connect — leaving the user with no path to recover state. Fix: (a) drop the AbortController from the initial-load effect — the `cancelled` flag already prevents stale state writes, the AbortController only adds the failure mode; (b) drop the initial-mount suppression in feature 11.1's resync effect — yes this causes a redundant GET on normal mount but it's idempotent + ~500 bytes, the trade-off for robustness is clearly worth it. Defense in depth: if initial-load completes, board syncs immediately; if initial-load is aborted (the bfcache case), resync recovers on first WS Connected; if both fail, STOMP MoveEvents catch up via existing applyOpponentMove path. Cross-repo: zero.
acceptance: src/pages/Play/Play.tsx initial-load effect drops the AbortController. The cleanup retains only `cancelled = true`. The async load handler still checks `cancelled` after the awaited getGameState call (and in the catch block) to suppress stale state writes when the component is no longer interested.

src/pages/Play/Play.tsx resync effect (feature 11.1) drops the initial-mount suppression. The guard previously gated on `previousConnectionState.current === null`. Now the resync fires on every transition INTO Connected, including the first one. Update the inline comment to reflect the new invariant: resync is always-on, robustness over deduplication.

Confirm via comment + test that the resync's GET response NEVER overwrites a newer state. The resync uses the same syncFromServer used by applyOpponentMove. If a STOMP MoveEvent arrived between the resync's GET dispatch and resolution, the resync's response would be older. Mitigation: keep the existing semantics (resync overwrites; this is intentional — the REST GET is the authoritative snapshot). Document this in the feature note.

Tests (Vitest): (1) simulate AbortError thrown by the mocked getGameState (initial-load aborted case) and verify the resync GET recovers state when connectionState transitions to Connected; (2) verify that on a successful initial-load, the resync STILL fires on first Connected and the second sync is idempotent (no visible regression); (3) verify the `cancelled` flag still prevents state writes when the component unmounts mid-fetch.

Tests Playwright: not feasible to simulate bfcache deterministically. Add a unit-level reproduction via mockStomp + MSW that mimics the abort + reconnect sequence. Document the Playwright skip rationale in the feature note.

title: Redirect /play to /new when there is no active room + remove stray Options label
description: Bug surfaced 2026-05-29 during a manual smoke test against the live site: opening /play directly (e.g. pasting https://chess-frontend-52i.pages.dev/play in a fresh tab) with no active room renders a dead-end phantom board — 'Waiting for opponent', 'Room ID: —', and the 'Guest' placeholder — with no roomId / gameId / playerId, so no one can ever join. There is no entry guard today (Play.tsx reads UserContext's RoomState discriminated union; the 'none' arm falls through and still paints the board). Fix: when Play mounts and room.phase === RoomPhase.None (no rehydrated session and no usable in-room state), redirect to /new with { replace: true } so the user lands on the configuration form instead of the dead-end board. Scope is the minimal redirect only — deep-link auto-join via ?roomId was explicitly considered and deferred by the user (would require POST /api/rooms/{id}/join or a spectator decision; tracked as a separate future feature). Also cleans up the stray 'Options' <Typography> label in the bottom-right of the board (Play.tsx:772) which has no handler and only headed the spectator-count chip, leaving 'Options' floating alone when viewerCount === 0. Inserted at priority 11.8, before board-themes (12).
acceptance: src/pages/Play/Play.tsx adds a mount-time entry guard: when room.phase === RoomPhase.None, redirect to /new with replace. The guard fires ONLY on the initial mount (e.g. ref-guarded like the existing reconciledRef, or a lazy useState capturing the initial phase + a render-time <Navigate to='/new' replace />). It must NOT react to post-mount transitions into 'none' that already navigate themselves (abandonment -> /home or /new via handleAbandonedHome/handleAbandonedNewGame; 404 / GAME_ALREADY_ENDED -> /new). No race with handleAbandonedHome's navigate('/home'). Implementer picks the cleaner spot; document the choice and why it avoids the race in the feature note.

No visible flash of the phantom board before the redirect: prefer a render-time <Navigate> (decided from the mount-time phase) over a post-paint useEffect, OR justify in the note why the useEffect approach does not flash. Either way 'replace: true' so Back does not return to the dead-end.

The URL-vs-stored reconciliation mismatch path (Play.tsx:134-152, currently leaveRoom() only) also redirects to /new with replace, since a fresh-entry without a session is itself a dead-end under the minimal scope (no deep-link join). Document this behavior change in the feature note.

Decision documented in the feature note: ?roomId in the URL without a valid in-room session does NOT auto-join (deep-link join was the deferred option-2 scope). phase === None redirects regardless of any ?roomId query param.

Remove the stray 'Options' <Typography> label (Play.tsx:772). The spectator-count Chip (rendered when viewerCount > 0) is preserved and rendered without a dangling empty header; its Tooltip and aria-label stay intact.

Tests (Vitest, src/pages/Play/Play.test.tsx): (a) mounting Play with room.phase === none redirects to /new with replace; (b) mounting with a valid in-room session renders the board and does NOT redirect; (c) non-regression: abandonment -> Home still navigates to /home (not /new); (d) the 'Options' label no longer renders, and the spectator chip still renders when viewerCount > 0.

Existing Vitest suite still passes (count may grow). RUN_E2E=true ./init.sh still passes: two-player.spec.ts enters via /new so the guard is a no-op there; no E2E change required unless a test happened to deep-link /play.
Bundle delta negligible; no new deps; no schema changes; openapi.json untouched.
./init.sh green end-to-end.
